solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copied flier found outside gym class

indicators.note: found outside means the flier's letters wrap around the gym class

parts.note: a flier is an advertising leaflet, an AD
PE is physical education, the school gym class

explanation.surface: Someone copied a leaflet they spotted outside a PE lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a bird or pilot, but here it is a handbill or advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, so the past tense is a synonym for copied.

clue.text: Two sharp double bends in valley, blind

indicators.note: in puts the doubled bends inside the word for valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England

indicators.note: Two asks for the bend-shaped letter to be written twice

parts.note: the letter Z is drawn like a road sign's sharp double bend

explanation.surface: A road-sign warning of hairpin bends down in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter Z looks like the road sign for a double bend, so two of them give ZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: To dazzle is to blind someone temporarily with bright light, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fed up by the end of Monday's challenge

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top
the end of picks out the final letter of Monday's

explanation.surface: Someone who has had enough of the challenge facing them at the end of Monday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as one idiom, but it splits into the word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy is to openly resist or dare someone, matching challenge as a verb.

clue.text: Perrin shows up after disturbing person on beach a lot?

indicators.note: disturbing means the letters of Perrin shows up are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Reginald Perrin, the sitcom character, turns up after something unsettling happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Reginald Perrin is the hero of a British sitcom who famously faked his death on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves sunbathing spends hours lying out on the sand, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Name large ship The Irishman

parts.note: to dub someone is to name them
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A man naming a great ship he calls The Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dubliner is a native of Dublin, Ireland's capital, so is a particular Irishman.

clue.text: Austere office contains record player

indicators.note: contains signals that the letters sit inside the phrase Austere office

explanation.surface: A bare, austere office that nonetheless has a record player in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system that plays records through two speakers.

clue.text: Girl to depart for city in US

parts.note: Sandie is a girl's name
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: A girl leaving for an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large Californian city near the Mexican border.

clue.text: High level leap, at different university

indicators.note: different means the letters of leap at are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A record high jump achieved at another university.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an elevated area of flat land, literally a high level.

clue.text: Extremist cult rarely demonstrates

indicators.note: demonstrates means the phrase cult rarely shows the letters within it

explanation.surface: An extreme cult seldom stages protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrates' suggests marching in protest; here it just means shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a noun meaning an extremist.

clue.text: Foolish using unknown quantities in do-it-yourself

indicators.note: in places the unknowns inside the home-improvement abbreviation

parts.note: in algebra z is an unknown quantity, so two of them give two Zs

explanation.surface: Doing home improvements without knowing the measurements is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy can mean scatterbrained or silly, as in a dizzy blonde.

clue.text: Chap making ref wild

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of ref wild are made into something new

explanation.surface: A man whose antics drive the referee mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred is a man's first name, so it is an example of a chap.

clue.text: Top person in sauna?

definitions.meaning: a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a jumper
someone in a sauna is perspiring heavily

explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted pullover, and also literally one who sweats, as anyone in a sauna does.

clue.text: Measure water source in place of nuclear power station

parts.note: size is a measure of how big something is
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Gauging a well's capacity at a nuclear plant site.
explanation.walkthrough: SIZEWELL is a village on the Suffolk coast of England, home to nuclear power stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizewell is the English coastal site best known for its nuclear reactors.

clue.text: Corner, note, or entrance to roof space?

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them
do is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Three options for reaching the loft, listed as alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged hatch set in a ceiling gives access to the loft above.

clue.text: Twelve people at the very end? An awful lot fewer!

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon

indicators.note: at the very end picks out the final letter of people

explanation.surface: A dozen arrive at the last moment, yet the crowd is far smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: nobody at all is indeed a lot fewer than twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody is the ultimate reduction in a headcount, about as few as possible.

clue.text: Frank the musician using sound from remote control

indicators.note: sound from says a word is said out loud and spelt as another

parts.note: a TV remote is informally called a zapper

explanation.surface: A musician called Frank operating a TV remote.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Zappa was an American rock guitarist and composer.

clue.text: Place on Russian mountain range in which sheep remains the same

definitions.text: in which sheep remains the same

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in street addresses
the Ural mountains run north to south through Russia

explanation.surface: Settling a flock on a Russian range where the sheep never change.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a grammar joke: the word sheep has the same form for one and many.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep is one of the nouns whose more-than-one form is unchanged from the singular.

clue.text: Hamlet's friend's house share not finalised

indicators.note: not finalised means the word for share loses its final letter

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A friend of Hamlet's has a house-share that isn't settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend and confidant in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Army of volunteers like unusual sort of film

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force of volunteers

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of like are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A volunteer army enjoys an odd kind of movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie is an early film with a soundtrack, as opposed to a silent picture.

clue.text: Cheerful after injury is concluded

indicators.note: after places the word for cheerful following the injury

parts.note: a wound is an injury
up can mean cheerful or happy

explanation.surface: Someone stays cheerful after getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is brought to an end it is said to be finished off, or wound up.

clue.text: Last character following Disney to dance

indicators.note: following puts the final letter after the name

parts.note: Walt Disney founded the film studio
Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The final cartoon character created by Disney steps out to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The waltz is a ballroom dance in triple time.

clue.text: Hit Western with bad actor

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts badly

explanation.surface: A cowboy film featuring a poor actor becomes a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham is a forceful blow, a noun or verb meaning a hit.

clue.text: Area of Eastern and Northern Australia looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: Parts of eastern and northern Australia doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' reads as improving prospects but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or district, a synonym of area.

clue.text: Backward about everything, it's plain

indicators.note: Backward means the pieces are written from right to left

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone behind the times on everything, saying it plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a wide grassy plain in Spanish-speaking South America.

clue.text: Dodging troubles so naive

indicators.note: troubles means the letters of so naive are stirred up

explanation.surface: Avoiding problems is such a naive approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is the act of avoiding or sidestepping, matching dodging as a noun.
